_about: Single source of every numeric band and method constant used by the harness,
meaning npm run verify and npm run gen:baseline. Each value carries a source.
'STAGE1.md check N' means the number is copied from the Verification checks table
or its method column. 'Loop A harness choice' means STAGE1.md left the number
unspecified and Loop A fixed it; the reasoning is in PROGRESS.md.
This file is owned by Loop A. Loop B must not edit it. Argue in PROGRESS.md instead.

canonical_render_hz.source: Loop A harness choice, canonical sim_step batching rate for the trace hash in checks 2 and 3

trace_stride_ms.source: Loop A harness choice, state block sampled into the trace every 10 ms

input_sample_hz.source: Loop A harness choice, inside the 125 to 1000 Hz HID report range in STAGE1.md input section

vendor_diff_chars.source: STAGE1.md check 1, git diff --stat vendor/betaflight empty

hash_mismatches.source: STAGE1.md check 2, two replays in one process hash identical
STAGE1.md check 3, Node and headless Chrome hashes identical

distinct_hashes.source: STAGE1.md check 4, all four traces identical

cell_voltage.source: STAGE1.md check 5 method, trim at 4.0 V per cell

cell_voltage.source: Loop A harness choice, full charge

throttle.source: Loop A harness choice, constant throttle during the roll, STAGE1.md check 10 method says constant throttle

roll_hold_s.source: Loop A harness choice, duration of the hard roll

min_abs_body_yaw_deg.source: Re-specified at the owner's request, argued in PROGRESS.md 2026-08-17. The old floor of 2.0 was recorded by its own source as a 'Loop A harness choice', and PROGRESS.md carries a three line proof that a symmetric QUADX cancels roll-to-yaw coupling EXACTLY, for any per-motor physics: reaching 2.0 deg would need about 44 deg of column asymmetry, and a well tuned quad does not yaw two degrees in a one second roll. What the plant models instead is explicit build tolerance, tangential motor cants of -0.9/+1.4/+0.6/-1.2 deg whose sum against the roll column is -1.1 deg, measured at -0.12 deg of drift over this maneuver. The floor is set where deleting that tolerance model (drift collapses toward 0.00, which is where this check sat for the project's whole life) fails loudly, with margin under the measured -0.12.

expected_sign.source: Loop A provisional choice for a positive (right) roll input with Betaflight props-in rotation. Sign convention: positive r yaws nose left. See PROGRESS.md OPEN QUESTIONS

max_abs_body_yaw_deg.source: The other half of the band, same argument. Coupling scales linearly with the cant table, so 0.60 deg is about five times the modeled build tolerance: someone inflating the invented cants to fake a bigger coupling, which is exactly how the old 2.0 floor would have had to be satisfied, fails this side. The check now guards the tolerance model from both directions instead of demanding a drift no physical quad exhibits.

cell_voltages.source: STAGE1.md check 11 method, identical punch-out at 4.20 and 3.60 V per cell

hover_settle_s.source: Loop A harness choice, same punch procedure as check 6

full_throttle_s.source: STAGE1.md check 6 method, reused so the two runs are the check 6 punch-out

band_percent.source: STAGE1.md check 11, low voltage peak RPM lower by 4 to 15 percent

cell_voltage.source: Loop A harness choice, full charge

throttle.source: Loop A harness choice, same procedure as check 9

hold_s.source: Loop A harness choice, same procedure as check 9

steady_window_s.source: Loop A harness choice, same procedure as check 9

audio-bed._about: The audio bed has to actually start. A user reported that no music played at all, and nothing in tests/ could have caught it: every audio claim in this project was measured by hand with scripts/audio-probe.js against a graph the probe builds itself, so the shell could stop building its own graph entirely and every check would still pass. These bound the live page instead.

min_music_gain._about: Music bus gain at the DEFAULT settings, with nothing touched. level 0.5 times the bed's 0.40 is 0.20, so 0.05 is a wide floor that still catches a silent or unattached bed.

min_music_steps._about: Sixteenth note steps the music scheduler must advance across a settled 4 s window. At 174 BPM that is 11.6 per second, so about 46. The window starts after a 1.5 s settle and runs 4 s rather than 1.5 because the scheduler advances in lookahead chunks: 1.5 s windows measured 23 and 20 steps, which imply 230 and 200 BPM on a 174 BPM bed, while 4 s averages to 11.49 per second or 172.4 BPM implied. 24 is a wide floor, about half the expected count, so it catches a stalled or half rate scheduler without asserting a tempo this counter cannot resolve; the tempo itself is measured off the rendered audio by scripts/audio-probe.js, at 173.64 BPM with r=0.4480 against a shuffled null p95 of 0.0378.

max_nodes._about: Web Audio nodes in the live graph. The budget is 64 and the graph builds 59, so this catches an unbounded voice pool without arguing about the exact count.

craft_body_m.source: The airframe's own published body length, 0.155 m front to back, measured off the drawn BoxGeometry. A 5 mm band because the number is authored, not sampled.

craft_sweep_m.source: Motor at 0.110 m from centre plus 0.0635 m of blade is 0.1735 m. The band spans a 200 to 250 mm class machine, which is what a 5 inch quad is.

craft_radius_tolerance_m.source: CRAFT_R must BE the swept disc, not approximate it: both are now derived from the same two numbers, so any gap at all is a regression. Half a millimetre is floating point slack.

gate_opening_m.source: MultiGP's published standard gate opening is 1.524 m square (5 ft) and src/game/track.js still says so. The course is BUILT at GATE_SCALE 1.15 times that, 1.7526 m, at the owner's explicit instruction that the gates be 15 percent larger; the band is that figure plus and minus 5 mm. scene.js already throws on a 10 mm drift at load; this is the independent check.

grass_blade_m.source: Mown chapter grass is 3 to 5 cm and MultiGP asks for a course as flat as possible; the build authors 0.03 to 0.09 m. The band is deliberately wide enough to accept a re-authoring and narrow enough that the 0.26 to 0.68 m error this project shipped would fail it.

clubhouse_verandah_m.source: An Australian sports pavilion verandah is 2.4 to 2.7 m of clear headroom at its outer edge, where the roof has fallen for drainage. The band is that figure opened to 2.1 and 3.0, wide enough to accept a re-authored roof pitch and narrow enough that a verandah a pilot could not fly under, or one built at a warehouse's scale, fails it. The measurement is the underside of the verandah roof COLLIDER less the top of the LANDABLE deck, both taken from the lists src/render/scene.js actually consumes, so it bands the clearance a craft meets rather than a number in the dimension table. It is here because the pavilion is the only object on the race field sized by a human instead of by MultiGP or by the airframe, and check 15 exists for exactly that class of error.

kerb_m.source: A real Japanese residential kerb face is 0.10 to 0.20 m. Measured as the step the town's own height query returns between carriageway and footway, which is the surface the craft lands on.

doorway_m.source: A Japanese residential entrance door is 1.90 to 2.10 m. Measured as the median world bounding box height of every mesh drawn with the front door material.

handrail_m.source: A handrail is 0.85 to 1.20 m above the walking surface. Measured off the collider list, so it is the height of the thing a quad actually hits.

boom_m.source: A Japanese level crossing boom sits 1.00 to 1.40 m above the road. Measured from the arm pivot's world position, and it is what src/maps/city/animation.js gives the boom collider.

world_scale.source: The world is modelled at 1 times the aircraft's own scale (src/render/frame.js WORLD_SCALE), so a metre in the physics is a metre in the world. It was 1.25 for one round, to answer a report that the drone read too large against the gate and the town. That was the wrong lever: dividing the craft's displacement cannot change the angle a gate subtends, so it made no gate any bigger and it made every course a quarter longer to fly, which is a quarter added to every lap time on the board. Apparent size belongs to the camera and was fixed there, in CAMERA_FOVS. The check divides this back out before banding the airframe, so it is the declared ratio the page has to agree with, not a tolerance.

collider_fit_max_trim_m.source: src/maps/city/index.js trims the town's walker keep-out rectangles onto the geometry they stand for, and no face may move further than the largest standoff the town authors, the 1.8 m flank in district.js. An earlier version without this cap chopped a 78.9 m lineside railing to 0.18 m, so the cap is the guard against the fit failing to understand a collider rather than a tuning knob.

gate_scale.source: The declared departure from the rulebook, src/game/track.js GATE_SCALE. Here so that changing how big a gate is has to be done in two places on purpose, rather than in one place by accident.

city_modules_min.source: The city's import closure is 59 vendored files plus index.js, animation.js, bake.js and references.js. A floor rather than an equality because the browser may serve some from cache within one page life; anything near this number means the graph really arrived.

p1.source: Re-measured after the clubhouse was added to both race maps, 1280 by 720, graphics high, same parked camera as every previous reading. Previous figures: P1 313, P2 895639, P5 69.8 MB, P10 27.4 MB, 170 meshes. WHAT MOVED AND WHY, each part measured rather than reasoned about. The pavilion is authored as ONE geometry wearing ONE cel material in vertex colours, so it lands in a single merger bucket: counted in the page, the material keyed 'clubhouse' is on exactly 1 mesh of 5622 vertices, 1874 triangles and 198 KB of attributes. That is the whole of the +1 mesh and the +1 draw call. A pavilion built the obvious way, with a roof material, a wall material, a brick material and a glass material, would have cost four buckets and eight calls. P2 FELL by 1566 triangles even though 1874 arrived, because the clubhouse stands on levelled ground that the scenery loop must keep clear: 1874 + 1566 = 3440 triangles of trees and rocks that used to be drawn where the terrace now is. Those objects are still BUILT and then discarded, so the world's single rng stream is untouched and every remaining tree, rock, cliff, flower and mountain in the valley is where it was. P5 and P10 are unchanged: no render target moved and 198 KB does not reach a tenth of a megabyte. THIS IS A RE-MEASURE, NOT A THRESHOLD LOOSENED TO GET A PASS. Every figure is still an exact equality with a zero tolerance, and the assertion the check is named for, that the field costs the same after a round trip through the city, is asserted against BOOT rather than against these constants and held exactly on this run: 314, 894073, 69.8, 27.4, 171 both times. The cel material clock walk now reads 45 at boot and 45 after, where it read 44 then 45 before. That difference was not a leak and the meshes, calls and bytes above all said so: it was the clubhouse's shader compiling somewhere between the two measurements, because Three compiles lazily and the pavilion stands 40 m off the racing line and is out of frame at the parked camera. src/render/scene.js now calls renderer.compile once at the end of the map build, which is worth doing on its own account, a shader stall at a random point in a timed lap is the one frame drop a racing simulator cannot have, and it makes this count a property of the world instead of a property of where the camera has been. See PROGRESS.md. RE-MEASURED AGAIN for the plaque on the clubhouse wall, the Clarke quote, which is the one textured surface on the building: P2 894073 to 894085, meshes 171 to 172, and P1, P5 and P10 all unchanged. The +12 triangles are the plate's bronze surround, which is a box in the pavilion's own vertex coloured geometry. The +1 mesh is the engraved plate itself, which has to be separate: it is the only surface here carrying a uv attribute, and it is the only mesh in the world with receiveShadow false, which the merger cannot express because it stamps receiveShadow on every bucket it flushes. P1 DID NOT MOVE AND THAT IS NOT THE SAME AS FREE. This figure is draw calls at one parked camera near gate 0, and the plaque faces +Z on the far side of the field, so it is frustum culled there. It costs one draw call on any frame that actually shows it. The plate also carries a 1024 by 512 canvas texture, which no budget in this check counts; the gate banners already work the same way. RE-MEASURED AGAIN after the world was re-authored as the club's own flying ground from two photographs the owner supplied: the lake, the six cliff landmarks and the four mountain rings are gone, the 420 scattered trees are now a treeline on the paddock boundary, and there is a waist high chain link fence round it. P1 314 to 306, P2 894085 to 1004039, P10 27.4 to 31.6 MB, P5 unchanged, meshes 172 to 169. DRAW CALLS AND MESHES FELL, which is the part worth reading: the water surface, the cliff material and one of the four ridge materials went, and the fence's two new buckets and the horizon's one did not make it back up. P2 IS UP 12.3 PERCENT AND THAT IS THE PRICE OF THE TREELINE. A scatter over 640 m of valley discarded most of what it drew, on the course or in the lake; a boundary band discards almost nothing, so the same 420 draws put far more trees on the screen, and they are drawn at about twice the size because the gums in the club's ground level photograph are 12 to 18 m and this tree topped out near 11. It was 1114831 before a trim: the background scatter dropped from 140 to 110 and, more usefully, the far trees and the horizon are drawn WITHOUT the inverted hull outline, which doubles a tree's geometry and buys nothing at 300 m where the post pass already inks the silhouette from depth. That one flag returned 110792 triangles and 4.9 MB. EVERY GATE IS WHERE IT WAS, checked by reading all fourteen positions before and after: the paddock is levelled to the same datum the racing corridor already sat on, so the course, the track record and every time posted against it are untouched by any of this. See PROGRESS.md. RE-MEASURED for the car park and its access road, which moved out of the pavilion's own frame and onto the paddock's eastern edge where the aerial has them: P2 1004039 to 1014135 and P10 31.6 to 32.0 MB. P1 AND THE MESH COUNT DID NOT MOVE AT ALL, 306 and 169, because both objects wear the same vertex coloured material the pavilion wears and the scenery merger buckets by material, so they merge into a bucket that already existed. That is the whole reason they are built with that material rather than one of their own. Gate positions read and compared again: identical.

meshes.source: Re-measured after the clubhouse was added to both race maps, 1280 by 720, graphics high, same parked camera as every previous reading. Previous figures: P1 313, P2 895639, P5 69.8 MB, P10 27.4 MB, 170 meshes. WHAT MOVED AND WHY, each part measured rather than reasoned about. The pavilion is authored as ONE geometry wearing ONE cel material in vertex colours, so it lands in a single merger bucket: counted in the page, the material keyed 'clubhouse' is on exactly 1 mesh of 5622 vertices, 1874 triangles and 198 KB of attributes. That is the whole of the +1 mesh and the +1 draw call. A pavilion built the obvious way, with a roof material, a wall material, a brick material and a glass material, would have cost four buckets and eight calls. P2 FELL by 1566 triangles even though 1874 arrived, because the clubhouse stands on levelled ground that the scenery loop must keep clear: 1874 + 1566 = 3440 triangles of trees and rocks that used to be drawn where the terrace now is. Those objects are still BUILT and then discarded, so the world's single rng stream is untouched and every remaining tree, rock, cliff, flower and mountain in the valley is where it was. P5 and P10 are unchanged: no render target moved and 198 KB does not reach a tenth of a megabyte. THIS IS A RE-MEASURE, NOT A THRESHOLD LOOSENED TO GET A PASS. Every figure is still an exact equality with a zero tolerance, and the assertion the check is named for, that the field costs the same after a round trip through the city, is asserted against BOOT rather than against these constants and held exactly on this run: 314, 894073, 69.8, 27.4, 171 both times. The cel material clock walk now reads 45 at boot and 45 after, where it read 44 then 45 before. That difference was not a leak and the meshes, calls and bytes above all said so: it was the clubhouse's shader compiling somewhere between the two measurements, because Three compiles lazily and the pavilion stands 40 m off the racing line and is out of frame at the parked camera. src/render/scene.js now calls renderer.compile once at the end of the map build, which is worth doing on its own account, a shader stall at a random point in a timed lap is the one frame drop a racing simulator cannot have, and it makes this count a property of the world instead of a property of where the camera has been. See PROGRESS.md. RE-MEASURED AGAIN for the plaque on the clubhouse wall, the Clarke quote, which is the one textured surface on the building: P2 894073 to 894085, meshes 171 to 172, and P1, P5 and P10 all unchanged. The +12 triangles are the plate's bronze surround, which is a box in the pavilion's own vertex coloured geometry. The +1 mesh is the engraved plate itself, which has to be separate: it is the only surface here carrying a uv attribute, and it is the only mesh in the world with receiveShadow false, which the merger cannot express because it stamps receiveShadow on every bucket it flushes.
